holidays.name: National Hug a Newsperson Day
holidays.description: A day for giving a heartfelt squeeze to the reporters, editors, and journalists who keep us informed, often while running on caffeine and deadlines.
holidays.origin: This unofficial observance grew out of a grassroots effort to show appreciation for working journalists and has circulated among holiday calendars as a lighthearted thank-you to the press.
holidays.funFact: Many journalists will tell you that a hug is a much nicer response than the usual angry email in the inbox.

holidays.name: National School Librarian Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the people who guard the books, shush the hallways, and secretly steer kids toward the one story that changes their life.
holidays.origin: Established by the American Association of School Librarians, it falls during National Library Week in April to recognize the essential work done by school library professionals.
holidays.funFact: The date is observed right around National Library Week, so librarians often get a whole week of appreciation, which is a lot of book puns.

holidays.name: International Carrot Day
holidays.description: A crunchy celebration of the humble orange root vegetable, which was not always orange. Fans eat carrot cake, carrot juice, and carrots straight from the bag.
holidays.origin: Carrot Day is an informal food observance promoted by vegetable lovers and food calendar enthusiasts to celebrate the nutritional and culinary versatility of the carrot.
holidays.funFact: Early cultivated carrots were purple and yellow; the familiar orange variety was developed by Dutch growers in the 1600s.

holidays.name: World Rat Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to appreciating rats, the clever, social, and surprisingly affectionate rodents that make wonderful pets and have a terrible public relations problem.
holidays.origin: Observed by rat fanciers and animal welfare groups, it was started to challenge the negative stereotypes of rats and promote responsible rat ownership and rescue.
holidays.funFact: Rats laugh when tickled, emitting ultrasonic giggles that humans cannot hear without special equipment.

holidays.name: Tell a Lie Day
holidays.description: A day when people are encouraged to fib in harmless, creative ways, like claiming you once wrestled a bear or invented the paperclip.
holidays.origin: This tongue-in-cheek unofficial holiday sits right after April Fools' Day, giving pranksters a second wind for tall tales and silly stories.
holidays.funFact: The holiday is best enjoyed with a rule that all lies must be revealed by the end of the day, or friendships may suffer.
